intelligence.human_view: A page does not have to be broken to be unreadable — it only has to be gray. Gray text is the quiet failure: nothing errors, nothing overflows, and every word costs a little effort to read, until the whole page feels unpleasant and nobody can say why. His ruling makes readability a law, not a preference: every text element high-contrast, readable at a glance, pleasant to read. White on black is the standard; gray is out — on the Dashboard as on the pricing page, and everywhere the system writes words to a human. If it is not easy to read, it is not pleasant, and if it is not pleasant, it is not done.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a storybook printed in light gray letters — you can read it if you squint, but it's no fun, and your eyes get tired. Dad says: "That looks terrible. Write it in bright white on black, so it's easy and pleasant to read." That's the rule now: no gray text anywhere on the Dashboard — every word bright and easy to read at a glance. If a word is hard to read, it fails.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, gray writing looks terrible, love — it's not easy to read and it's not pleasant, and every word is a little effort. His ruling is simple, dear: no gray text anywhere on the Dashboard — every word bright white on black, easy to read at a glance, pleasant to read. Information is never written in gray, love — never small and faded and hard to see. If a word is hard to read, dear, it fails — that's the law now, for the whole system.
